info.title: Routebase Public API
info.description:
This reference covers the part of the Routebase API that is a commitment to
customers. Every endpoint here is called by a shipped Routebase client, so it is
already a contract in practice. The test CLI on nuget.org drives the CI, spec,
security and docs-as-code groups, and identity providers such as Okta and
Microsoft Entra drive the SCIM group.

Everything else under `/api/**` serves the Routebase web app, can change without
notice, and should not be built against.

The API is not versioned by path, and the version above numbers this document
rather than the API. A breaking change here is announced in the release notes
before it ships.

## Authentication

Send an API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Keys are created under Settings then
API Keys, they start with `rb_live_`, and each one carries its own permission
scopes and an optional restriction to a single project. A scoped key cannot reach
organization level operations at all, so grant the least privilege that works.

SCIM is the exception and authenticates with a separate bearer token, issued per
organization when SCIM provisioning is enabled.

## Regions

An organization lives in exactly one region. US organizations must send the
`X-RB-Region` header documented on every operation, otherwise the request is
routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

## Rate limits

Requests are counted in a rolling window of 60 seconds. A call authenticated with
an API key gets 100 requests per window, counted per user of that key. SCIM is
counted per source IP instead, so every call from one identity provider shares a
single budget. Exceeding it answers `429` with a `Retry-After` header, which a
polling CI job should honour rather than retry immediately.

## Errors

Failures return `application/problem+json` with a machine readable `code` field.
Read that rather than the human readable `detail`, which may be reworded. SCIM
endpoints return the SCIM error envelope instead. Every identifier in this API is
a public UUID.

get.summary: List the environments of a project
get.description:
Returns the environments of a project, so a pipeline can pick the one whose
variables the run should use. An environment marked `isReadOnly` rejects every
write request sent to it, and the test cases concerned are reported as blocked
rather than failed.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

post.summary: Run a test suite and wait for the result
post.description:
Executes a test suite and returns the outcome in one call, which is what a
pipeline step needs. The response tells you whether everything passed, so a
CI job can fail on `allPassed` alone. Pass a `reportFormat` to get the report
inline instead of downloading it separately.

The call blocks until the run finishes. For a long suite, send `progressRunId`
and poll the status endpoint instead of holding the connection open.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

200.description: The run completed. Check `allPassed` for the verdict.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: Download the report of a finished run
get.description:
Returns the run report as a file. JUnit XML is the default because GitHub
Actions, Azure Pipelines and Jenkins all read it natively.

The run has to be finished. Asking for the report of a pending or running test
run is answered with 409, so poll the status endpoint first.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Report format. Defaults to `junit`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Public id of the test run.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

409.description: The run is still pending or running, so there is no report yet.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: Get the progress of a test run
get.description:
Returns how far a run has come, which lets a pipeline show progress instead of
waiting silently. While the run is going, `currentDurationMs` counts up and
`completedAt` stays null.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Public id of the test run.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

200.description: The current status of the run.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: List the test suites of a project
get.description: Returns the test suites of a project so a pipeline can resolve a suite by name.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: List the documentations of a project
get.description:
Returns the documentations of a project with their versions, which is how a
pipeline finds the id of the version it should write into. Only a version whose
status is `draft` or `review` accepts changes, so pick one of those.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

post.description:
Creates a folder in a version. A folder with `isSection` set becomes a top level
section in the portal header rather than an entry in the sidebar, and only a
folder at the root can be one.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

post.description:
Creates a page inside a version, at the root or under a folder. The slug is
derived from the title when you do not send one, and it is what the public
portal URL is built from, so set it explicitly if the URL matters to you.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: Get a page with its content
get.description:
Returns one page including its Markdown content and its `rowVersion`. Send that
`rowVersion` back on the next update and a concurrent edit is rejected with 409
instead of silently overwriting someone else's work.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

put.description:
Replaces the title and content of a page, which is the call that carries a
Markdown file from your repository into Routebase. A page that a person has
locked in the editor is not writable, and the call is rejected until the lock is
released.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: Get the page tree of a version
get.description:
Returns the full hierarchy of a documentation version. Each node is exactly one
of a page, a folder or an API reference snapshot, and the `type` field says
which of the three is filled.

The response carries an ETag, so a pipeline that syncs repeatedly can send
`If-None-Match` and skip the work when nothing moved.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

304.description: Nothing changed since the ETag you sent.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

put.summary: Reorder the items under one parent
put.description:
Sets the order of the items inside one folder, or at the root when
`parentFolderPublicId` is null. Send the complete list of ids in the order you
want, because the position of an item is its index in that list.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: List security findings
get.description:
Returns the findings of a project across all scans, filtered as you need them.
A pipeline that only wants to know whether anything new broke should filter on
`status=open` and on the severities it cares about.

parameters.name: assignedToMe
parameters.description: Return only findings assigned to the calling user.

parameters.name: scannerId
parameters.description: Filter by the scanner that produced the finding.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search across title and description.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Filter by severity.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Sort order of the result.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by finding status.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: Export findings as SARIF
get.description:
Returns the findings of a project as a SARIF 2.1.0 document, which GitHub code
scanning and comparable tools ingest directly. Upload it from your pipeline and
the findings show up next to the code they concern. Without a `status` filter it
returns the open ones, which is what a build gate wants.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by finding status. Defaults to `open`.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

post.description:
Queues a scan for the given profile and returns immediately with the tracking id,
because a scan runs in the background. Poll the scan run endpoint until its
status leaves `queued` and `running`.

parameters.name: profileId
parameters.description: Public id of the scan profile.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

Location.description: URL of the scan run to poll.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: Get a scan run
get.description:
Returns the state of a scan, including how many scanners have finished and which
one is running. Once `status` is `completed`, `securityScore` and
`openFindingsCount` are final and a pipeline can gate on them.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Public id of the scan run.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: List the specifications of a project
get.description:
Returns the specifications of a project together with the number of their
latest published version, so a pipeline can resolve a spec by name and see at a
glance what is live.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: Export the current state of a specification
get.description:
Returns the working state of a specification as OpenAPI, which is the draft as
it stands in the designer right now. To export something stable, export a
published version instead.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: List the versions of a specification
get.description:
Returns the versions of a specification with their status and publish target.
Only a version whose status is `published` is frozen, so anything else can still
change underneath you.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: Export a published version
get.description:
Returns a published version as a downloadable OpenAPI document. A published
version is frozen, so the same call returns the same bytes forever, which makes
it safe to generate clients from in a build.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

200.description: The specification document as a file.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

post.summary: Record that a version went into an environment
post.description:
Tells Routebase which version an environment now serves. The intended order is
that your pipeline deploys first and then makes this call, so the pin reflects
what is actually running rather than what someone intended.

A call authenticated with an API key is recorded with source `cli`, which is how
a pipeline assertion is told apart from someone clicking in the UI. If the target
environment freezes versions, the promoted version becomes immutable here.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

409.description:
The promotion is blocked. The most common reason is an unacknowledged impact
on dependent services, which you clear by sending `impactAcknowledged`.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: List the test suites of a project
get.description:
The project scoped equivalent of `/api/cli/suites`, which returns the same page
of suites. Use whichever fits the path style of your client.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

post.description:
Runs every test case in a suite in order, carrying extracted variables from one
case into the next. This is the full result shape, so it also carries the
per-case detail, the seed results and the performance metrics that
`/api/cli/run` leaves out.

Set `persistResults` to false for a dry run that leaves no test run behind.

parameters.name: suiteId
parameters.description: Public id of the test suite.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait.

get.summary: List groups
get.description:
Returns the provisioned groups of an organization in a SCIM ListResponse
envelope. Groups map onto Routebase teams, and a group mapping decides which
role its members receive.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: SCIM filter expression, for example `displayName eq "Engineering"`.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

post.description: Creates a group and adds the members you send with it.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

get.summary: Get a group
get.description: Returns one provisioned group with its members.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

patch.description:
Applies a SCIM PatchOp to a group, which is how an identity provider adds and
removes members as people join and leave a team.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

delete.description: Removes a group. Its members keep their organization membership.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

get.summary: List the supported resource types
get.description: Returns the SCIM resource types this service exposes, which are User and Group.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

get.summary: List the supported schemas
get.description: Returns the SCIM schemas backing the User and Group resources.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

get.summary: Describe what this SCIM service supports
get.description:
Returns the SCIM service provider configuration, which identity providers read
during setup to learn which operations are available.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

get.summary: List users
get.description:
Returns the provisioned users of an organization in a SCIM ListResponse
envelope. Identity providers use the `filter` parameter to look a user up by
`userName` before deciding whether to create or update.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: SCIM filter expression, for example `userName eq "ada@example.com"`.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

post.description:
Creates a user in the organization. A user provisioned this way joins with the
default member role, and further role changes stay with Routebase rather than
the identity provider.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

get.summary: Get a user
get.description: Returns one provisioned user.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

put.description:
Replaces the attributes of a user wholesale. Attributes you leave out are
cleared, so send the complete resource rather than a partial one.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

patch.description:
Applies a SCIM PatchOp to a user. This is the call an identity provider makes to
deactivate someone, by setting `active` to false, which is a soft removal that
keeps the audit trail intact.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

delete.description: Removes a user from the organization.

parameters.name: X-RB-Region
parameters.description: Region of your organization. US organizations must send `us`; EU organizations leave the header out. Without it a US call is routed to the EU region and answered with 401.

429.description: The rate limit was exceeded. The `Retry-After` header gives the seconds to wait. SCIM is counted per source IP.

type.description: A URI identifying the problem type.

title.description: A short summary of the problem type.

instance.description: The path that produced the error.

code.description:
The stable machine readable error code, for example `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT`,
`PROJECT_LOCKED`, `API_KEY_SCOPE_DENIED` or `NOT_A_MEMBER`.

Problem.description:
The error shape of the API, which follows RFC 9457. Branch on `code`, because
`detail` is written for people and may be reworded.

Severity.description: How serious a security finding is.

Confidence.description: How certain the scanner is that a finding is real.

FindingStatus.description: Where a finding stands in triage.

ScanStatus.description: The lifecycle state of a scan run.

VersionStatus.description:
The lifecycle state of a specification version. Only `published` is frozen and
therefore safe to generate clients from.

PublishTarget.description: Who a published version is visible to.

OpenApiVersion.description: The OpenAPI dialect of a specification.

EnvironmentType.description: The stage an environment stands for.

PinSource.description:
Where a version pin came from. A call authenticated with an API key is recorded
as `cli`, which marks it as a pipeline assertion rather than a manual entry.

OnErrorBehavior.description:
What a run does when a test case errors. `ignore` continues, `stop` ends the
current iteration but starts the next one, and `abort` ends the whole run.

DocPageType.description: The template a documentation page was created from.

DocVersionStatus.description:
The lifecycle state of a documentation version. Only `draft` and `review` accept
content changes.

DocVisibility.description: Who can read a published documentation version.

VersionNumberingScheme.description: How a documentation numbers its versions.

suiteId.description: Public id of the test suite to run.

environmentId.description: Environment whose variables the run substitutes.

iterations.description: How often to run the suite, between 1 and 10000. Defaults to 1.

delayMs.description: Pause between iterations in milliseconds, up to 60000. Defaults to 0.

reportFormat.description: Include the report inline in the response in this format. Omit it to get no report.

threads.description:
Parallel threads for performance mode, between 1 and 50. Defaults to 1,
which runs the cases in order and carries variables between them.

authOverrideJson.description:
Authentication configuration that replaces the one stored on the suite,
which lets a pipeline inject its own credentials.

CliRunRequest.description: Everything a pipeline needs to start one suite run.

allPassed.description: Whether every test case passed across every iteration. Gate your build on this.

testRunId.description: Public id of the stored test run, which the report endpoints take.

iterationResults.description: Per-iteration breakdown, present only when more than one iteration ran.

report.description: The report content, present only when `reportFormat` was requested.

reportContentType.description: MIME type of the inline report.

CliRunResponse.description: The verdict of a suite run, shaped for a CI step. Branch your build on allPassed.

id.description: Public id of the test run.

currentDurationMs.description: Elapsed time, which counts up while the run is going and is final once it ends.

completedAt.description: When the run ended, or null while it is still going.

CliRunStatus.description: How far a running suite has come, for progress output while a run is in flight.

environmentId.description: Environment whose variables the run substitutes.

persistResults.description: Whether to store the run and its results. Defaults to true.

iterations.description: How often to run the suite, between 1 and 10000. Defaults to 1.

delayMs.description: Pause between iterations in milliseconds, up to 60000. Defaults to 0.

dataSetId.description: Data set for data-driven execution, which runs every case once per row.

threads.description: Parallel threads for performance mode, between 1 and 50. Defaults to 1.

progressRunId.description:
Client-generated id for live progress. Join the test-runner hub group for
this id before sending the request, then follow the run case by case.

caseIds.description: Run only these test cases. Null or empty runs the whole suite.

ExecuteTestSuiteRequest.description: Options for a suite run. Every field has a default, so the body may be omitted entirely.

results.description: One entry per test case execution, in run order.

extractedVariables.description: Variables extracted during the run and carried between cases.

testRunPublicId.description: Public id of the stored run, or null when results were not persisted.

iterationResults.description: Per-iteration breakdown, present only when more than one iteration ran.

dataSetName.description: Name of the data set, for a data-driven run.

performanceMetrics.description: Timing distribution, present when the run used more than one thread or iteration.

preRunSeedResult.description: Result of the seed that ran before the suite.

postRunSeedResult.description: Result of the seed that ran after the suite.

resetSnapshotResult.description: Result of the snapshot restore that ran before the suite.

TestSuiteExecutionResult.description: The full result of a suite run, including per-case detail, seeds and performance figures.

results.description: The result of every test case in this iteration, in run order.

allPassed.description: Whether every case passed in this iteration.

wasAborted.description: Whether the iteration stopped early because of the error behaviour.

dataRowIndex.description: The 0-based data row, for a data-driven run.

dataRowValues.description: The data row values used, for a data-driven run.

IterationResult.description: One pass over the suite, for runs configured with more than one iteration or a data set.

statusCode.description: Status code from the target server, or 0 when the request never went out.

statusText.description: Reason phrase from the target server.

headers.description: Response headers from the target server.

body.description: Response body, which may be null for an empty response.

error.description: Set when the request itself failed, for example on a timeout.

unresolvedVariables.description: Variables that could not be resolved, which is usually a missing environment value.

passed.description: Whether every assertion held. Null when the case has no assertions or never ran.

assertionResults.description: One entry per assertion on the case. Null when the case carries none or never ran.

testCaseId.description: Public id of the test case.

extractedVariables.description: Variables this response contributed to later cases.

preRequestScriptOutput.description: Console output of the pre-request script.

preRequestScriptError.description: Set when the pre-request script failed.

postResponseScriptOutput.description: Console output of the post-response script.

postResponseScriptError.description: Set when the post-response script failed.

timingBreakdown.description: Where the time went inside the request.

isPending.description: The case has not run yet.

isBlocked.description:
The case was never sent, because it writes and the environment is read-only.
This is neither a pass nor a failure, so do not fail a build on it alone.

TestCaseExecutionResult.description: What happened to one test case: the response it got, the assertions it checked, and the variables it passed on.

assertionId.description: Public id of the assertion, stable across runs.

type.description: What the assertion checks, for example the status code or a JSON path.

operator.description: How expected and actual are compared.

target.description: What the assertion points at, for example a JSON path.

expectedValue.description: The value the assertion demanded, rendered as text.

actualValue.description: The value the response actually carried, rendered as text.

checkedVersionNumber.description: Specification version the contract assertion checked against.

driftedFromVersionNumber.description: Set when the response no longer matches the version it used to.

AssertionResult.description: The outcome of one assertion, with expected and actual side by side.

dnsMs.description: Time spent resolving the hostname. Zero on a reused connection.

connectMs.description: Time spent opening the TCP connection.

tlsMs.description: Time spent on the TLS handshake.

firstByteMs.description: Time from request sent to the first response byte, which is where server work shows up.

downloadMs.description: Time spent reading the response body.

totalMs.description: Total wall time of the request. It covers the phases above plus scheduling overhead.

TimingBreakdown.description: Where the time inside one request went, from name resolution to the last byte.

averageResponseTimeMs.description: Mean response time across every request in the run.

minResponseTimeMs.description: Fastest single response in the run.

maxResponseTimeMs.description: Slowest single response in the run, which is the number a timeout budget has to beat.

medianResponseTimeMs.description: Median response time, less distorted by outliers than the mean.

p95ResponseTimeMs.description: 95th percentile, so one request in twenty was slower than this.

p99ResponseTimeMs.description: 99th percentile, the usual number behind a latency commitment.

throughputPerSecond.description: Completed requests per second across the run.

errorRatePercent.description: Share of requests that failed, from 0 to 100.

totalRequests.description: Requests sent across all threads and iterations.

successfulRequests.description: Requests that completed and passed their assertions.

failedRequests.description: Requests that errored or failed an assertion.

perTestCase.description: The same figures broken down per test case, which is how you find the one slow call.

PerformanceMetrics.description: Latency distribution and throughput of a run. Present once a run used parallel threads or several iterations.

testCaseId.description: Public id of the test case these figures belong to.

testCaseName.description: Display name of the test case.

averageResponseTimeMs.description: Mean response time of this case across all its executions.

p95ResponseTimeMs.description: 95th percentile response time of this case.

errorRatePercent.description: Share of this case executions that failed, from 0 to 100.

requestCount.description: How often this case ran, which is iterations multiplied by threads.

TestCasePerformance.description: Latency figures for a single test case across all its executions.

success.description: Whether every step of the seed completed. A failed seed does not stop the suite by itself.

elapsedMilliseconds.description: Duration of the whole seed sequence.

stepResults.description: One entry per seed step, in execution order.

capturedVariables.description: Variables the seed captured for the suite that follows.

error.description: Why the seed failed. Null on success.

SeedExecutionResult.description: The outcome of a seed sequence, which prepares data before a suite or cleans up after it.

order.description: Position of the step in the sequence, starting at 1.

statusCode.description: HTTP status the step received. Null for steps that send no request.

error.description: Why the step failed. Null on success.

resolvedMethod.description: The HTTP method the step used.

iterationIndex.description: Which repetition this is, for a step configured to loop.

capturedVariables.description: Variables this step captured for the steps and cases that follow.

SeedStepResult.description: One step inside a seed sequence.

success.description: Whether the environment was restored to the snapshot state.

cleanupResults.description: One entry per cleanup call, in execution order.

reSeedResult.description: Result of the seed that repopulated the environment after cleanup. Null when none ran.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems, such as a cleanup call that found nothing to delete.

error.description: Why the restore failed. Null on success.

SnapshotRestoreResult.description: The outcome of restoring an environment to a known state before a run.

order.description: Position of the cleanup call in the sequence, starting at 1.

method.description: HTTP method of the cleanup call, usually DELETE.

url.description: The URL the cleanup call went to.

statusCode.description: HTTP status the cleanup call received.

error.description: Why the cleanup call failed. Null on success.

SnapshotCleanupStepResult.description: One cleanup call inside a snapshot restore.

items.description: The test suites on this page.

name.description: Display name of the suite, which is what the CLI resolves when you pass a name.

tags.description: Labels used to group and filter suites.

testCaseCount.description: How many test cases the suite holds.

authMode.description: How the suite authenticates against the target API.

testSuiteFolderId.description: Folder the suite sits in, or null at the root.

type.description: Which stage the environment stands for.

baseUrl.description: Base URL requests in this environment are sent to.

createdAt.description: When the environment was created, in UTC.

variableCount.description: How many variables the environment defines for substitution.

freezesVersion.description: A promotion into this environment makes the promoted version immutable.

isDocsSource.description: What this environment pins is what the public documentation shows.

isMockSource.description: What this environment pins is what the mock server serves.

isReadOnly.description:
Only GET, HEAD and OPTIONS may be sent here. Test cases that write are

name.description: Display name of the specification, which is what the CLI resolves when you pass a name.

version.description: The version string carried in the document itself.

totalCount.description: Total number of versions of this specification, ignoring paging.

versionNumber.description: The version label, for example 1.2.0. It follows the numbering scheme of the organization.

status.description: Where the version stands in its lifecycle.

publishedAt.description: When the version was published, in UTC. Null while it is still a draft or in review.

publishTarget.description: Who the version is visible to. Null until it is published.

environmentId.description: Environment the version was deployed to.

Confirms you have seen the effect on dependent services. Send true to clear

faviconUrl.description: Icon shown in the browser tab.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or failed validation.

Unauthorized.description:
The API key is missing, invalid, expired or revoked. A US organization calling
without `X-RB-Region: us` also lands here, because the request reached the wrong
region.

Forbidden.description:
The key is valid but lacks the permission or the project scope for this call.
A scoped key is also refused on organization level operations by design.

NotFound.description:
The resource does not exist, or it belongs to another organization or project.
Both cases answer the same way on purpose, so the API cannot be used to probe
for foreign identifiers.

Conflict.description:
The resource changed since you read it. Reload it, reapply your change and send
the fresh `rowVersion`. The `code` is `CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT`.

tags.name: CI & Test Runs
tags.description:
Run test suites from a pipeline and collect the result. These endpoints back the
`routebase` CLI and the Routebase GitHub Action, and they are the ones a CI job
calls directly.

tags.name: API Specs
tags.description:
Read specifications and their versions, export them as OpenAPI, and record which
version a deployment put into an environment.

tags.name: Security
tags.description:
Start an OWASP scan, poll it to completion, and read the findings. The SARIF
export feeds GitHub code scanning and comparable tools.

tags.name: Docs as Code
tags.description:
Keep documentation pages in your own repository and push them into Routebase from
a pipeline. These endpoints back `routebase docs push` and `routebase docs pull`.

tags.name: SCIM
tags.description:
SCIM 2.0 user and group provisioning, as consumed by Okta, Microsoft Entra ID and
other identity providers. Available on plans that include SSO.
